correctness.rationale: Directly reconstructed multiplicative expansions: equal increments force equality of first and second elementary symmetric sums of two distinct prime triples. Subtracting their monic cubics gives constant h and disjoint prime supports. Parity forces all six primes odd. Normalizing the globally least prime t to the first triple yields even offsets (0,u,v),(a,b,c), with a<b<c, h=abc, and the required positive square discriminant (a+b+c)^2-4(ab+ac+bc)=(v-u)^2. For h<320 the strict offset-product inequality exhausts exactly 37 triples and leaves just two nondegenerate square shapes, at h=96 and 192; each covers all residues modulo 3 and is impossible for t>3; t=3 gives a composite 15 or 9. The six claimed witness factors are prime, their pair sums agree, and phi/sigma jumps both equal 320. Independent integer program enumerated all 37 constrained shapes and verified the two impossibilities and witness. Finite search proves the universal exclusion only because the algebraic normalization bounds all candidate offset triples.
